purpose: Teach: 親しく/ノック/バレンタイン/小児科/丸ごと/ひととき/救っ/かなわ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ご近所さん、親しくしてくださって、本当に、ありがたいな、ばあさん。
lines.en: The neighbors have been so kind to us. I'm really grateful, you know.
lines.style: Gentle, warm opening. Quiet conviction underneath. Slow, measured pace. Slight catch on 'grateful'—genuine emotion crossing his face. Voice settles at the end like a sigh of contentment.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。玄関の、ノックの音、最近、よく聞こえるようになったわね、年だわ。
lines.en: Yes. Funny—I hear the knock at the door so much lately. Getting old, aren't we.
lines.style: Soft laugh underneath. Matter-of-fact but affectionate. Pace slightly wry. A small pause after 'door'—noticing her own aging without dwelling on it. Trailing acceptance in the last phrase.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: バレンタインの日、若い頃、ばあさん、チョコ、くれたな、覚えてる、私?
lines.en: Valentine's Day, when you were younger—you gave me chocolate, remember? I still do.
lines.style: Eyes distant. Warm smile in the voice. Slow, dreamy pace. Gentle emphasis on 'chocolate'—the small sweetness of it. Voice trails slightly, almost asking permission to remember.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 孫、最近、熱、よく出すから、小児科、頻繁に、行ってるみたいね、息子、大変。
lines.en: Your grandson's been running fevers a lot lately. Seems like your son's at the pediatrician constantly. That's been hard on him.
lines.style: Shift to practical concern. Lower register. Eye contact steady. The worry is real but delivered with the matter-of-factness of someone used to managing family troubles. Slight weight on 'hard'.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、スイカ、丸ごと、食べたな、夏は、よく、楽しかった。
lines.en: When I was young, my grandfather would eat watermelon whole in the summer. Those were good days—so much fun.
lines.style: Distant, warmth underlying. Slower tempo. Visual memory in the voice—he's seeing it. Slight smile on 'whole.' Fades gently on 'fun,' like he's checking the feeling is still there.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 庭で、ひととき、お茶を飲む時間、二人の、贅沢な時間ね、いつも。
lines.en: In the garden, those moments with tea—just the two of us. It's our luxury, isn't it. Always has been.
lines.style: Tender, almost reverent. Soft attack. Gentle pace that lets each phrase breathe. On 'luxury,' warmth and gratitude curve upward slightly. Lands firmly on 'always'—this is bedrock.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 戦時中、命を救ってくれた医師、今でも、感謝しているよ、私、ばあさん。
lines.en: During the war, there was a doctor who saved my life. I think of him often, and I'm grateful. You know that.
lines.style: Serious, grounded shift. Weight on 'saved.' Pause after 'often'—honoring the memory. Quiet reverence, not heavy. Voice settles with purpose. Final phrase is steady, a truth being stated plainly.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: あなたの料理の腕、最近、私には、もう、かなわないわよ、上達したわね。
lines.en: Your cooking has gotten so good lately—I can't match you anymore. You've really improved.
lines.style: Pride breaking through. Warm, admiring tone. Light, almost playful opening. Pause on 'can't match'—a gentle surrender, not a complaint. Closes with genuine affection underneath.
